acceptance_criteria.criterion: dotnet build produces zero errors and zero warnings.
Old toolbar controls (ShowLibraryFoldersCommand button, RefreshIndex button, Search TextBox, Filter ComboBox, indexed count TextBlock) absent from MainContentView.axaml.
No SelectedItem attribute or binding on the NavigationView element.
IPrimaryNavigationService resolved via App.Services in constructor; SelectionChanged and ActiveDestinationChanged handlers both present.
Programmatic navigation updates IsSelected state on correct NavigationViewItem.

summary: WP-011 implementation was already complete upon inspection. MainContentView.axaml uses a FluentAvalonia NavigationView rail (PaneDisplayMode=Left) with no SelectedItem attribute and no legacy toolbar controls. Code-behind resolves IPrimaryNavigationService via App.Services, subscribes to SelectionChanged and ActiveDestinationChanged, and programmatically sets IsSelected on the correct NavigationViewItem via UpdateSelectedItem(). Build produces zero errors; the sole MSB3061 warning is a file-lock artifact from a concurrent test process, not a compiler warning.

comments.note: MainContentView.axaml.cs: UpdateSelectedItem sets NavView.Header from _primaryNavService.Destinations — if a destination Id is valid but not found in Destinations (e.g., stale Tag value), Header silently becomes null. A defensive fallback (e.g., retaining prior header value) would be more robust but is low priority since all destination Tags are hardcoded.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified. Build: 0 errors, 0 warnings. MainContentView.axaml contains only NavigationView + ContentControl — no legacy toolbar controls. NavigationView has no SelectedItem attribute or binding. Code-behind resolves IPrimaryNavigationService via App.Services; both SelectionChanged and ActiveDestinationChanged handlers are present and correct. UpdateSelectedItem() iterates MenuItems and sets IsSelected via Tag match — programmatic sync is correct. Full test suite: 680 passed (223 + 288 + 169), 6 skipped (infrastructure live-DB tests), 0 failed. No regressions detected.

metrics.test_coverage: Full suite run across all three test projects

comments.note: MainContentView.axaml.cs UpdateSelectedItem(): _updatingSelection guard correctly prevents re-entrant SelectionChanged dispatch during programmatic IsSelected assignment. Pattern is clean and race-condition-free.
MainContentView.axaml.cs OnUnloaded(): ActiveDestinationChanged is correctly unsubscribed, preventing memory leaks when the view is removed from the visual tree.

MainContentView.axaml.cs UpdateSelectedItem(): If destinationId does not match any NavigationViewItem Tag, all IsSelected become false and NavView.Header becomes null. Developer already noted this; acceptable given all Tags are hardcoded constants.

summary: Code review passed with no blocking issues.

MainContentView.axaml is clean: NavigationView with PaneDisplayMode=Left, five NavigationViewItems with Tag attributes, ContentControl bound to CurrentChildViewModel, no SelectedItem attribute, no legacy toolbar controls.

MainContentView.axaml.cs: service locator pattern in constructor is the required Avalonia pattern (acknowledged by comment). _updatingSelection bool guard is correct for single-threaded UI dispatch; try/finally guarantees reset on exception. OnUnloaded correctly unsubscribes ActiveDestinationChanged. StringComparison.Ordinal used appropriately for opaque ID strings.
PrimaryNavigationService implementation is correct: foreach loop avoids LINQ allocation, idempotency guard on NavigateTo is clean.
One documentation-forward note filed for the test-constructor comment.

comments.note: MainContentView.axaml.cs: The two-pass approach in UpdateSelectedItem (foreach for IsSelected, then FirstOrDefault for Header) could theoretically be merged into one loop, but given 5 constant items there is no meaningful performance impact. No change required.

[documentation-forward] MainContentView.axaml.cs: The MainContentView(MainContentViewModel viewModel) constructor comment says 'Available for direct instantiation (e.g., in test scenarios)' but the chain to this() means App.Services must be initialized for the call to succeed. The comment should clarify that this constructor is only safe in environments where the Avalonia headless application (and App.Services) is initialized — e.g., via Avalonia.Headless.XUnit — and is not safe in pure-unit-test contexts.

summary: Addressed the documentation-forward note from code review: updated the MainContentView(MainContentViewModel viewModel) constructor comment to clarify it is only safe in Avalonia.Headless.XUnit test environments where App.Services is initialized, and not safe in pure unit-test contexts.
